Keep `Order.totalMinor` as an integer and retain the existing `http` client. The supplied facts establish that both the API and receipt export depend on integer minor units; neither a model-type change nor a networking migration is authorized.

Apply the workflow with focused responsibilities, using the supplied context only:

| Owner | Responsibility and handoff |
|---|---|
| Workflow coordinator | Own the feature’s acceptance criteria, shared contracts, integration, and bounded final review. Resolve proposals against the authorized scope. |
| UI | Render a localized currency label derived from `totalMinor`. Pass formatting requirements and expected labels to state and testing owners; keep presentation strings out of the shared monetary contract. |
| ChangeNotifier state | Coordinate confirmation, expose the order and relevant loading/error states, and notify the UI. Preserve integer amounts through state transitions. |
| Repository | Preserve the order contract between state and transport. Pass confirmed response fields and error behavior to the state owner. |
| HTTP | Use the existing `http` client. Preserve integer serialization/parsing for `totalMinor`; provide response and failure fixtures for repository tests. |
| Tests and review | Exercise the coherent path across HTTP, repository, notifier, and UI, and check receipt-export compatibility where the change reaches it. Review only the task diff and directly affected consumers. |

The impact map follows the amount through each boundary: HTTP parsing must produce an integer; the repository and notifier must preserve it; UI formatting must derive a label without mutating it; receipt export must still receive integer minor units. The exact parser, repository methods, notifier transitions, UI formatter, and export regression assertions still require inspection. Currency identity, minor-unit scale, locale selection, and rounding conventions also need confirmation from existing contracts and conventions before implementing formatting that depends on them.

Reject the UI proposal to replace `totalMinor` with a string because it breaks established shared consumers. Redirect it to presentation formatting. Reject the Dio migration because it expands scope without a demonstrated requirement. Specialists should exchange contract details, fixtures, state transitions, and expected assertions—not independently redefine shared types or infrastructure. No specialist loading or delegation has occurred here.

Implementation can proceed once those remaining design-relevant details are confirmed, using the existing architecture and packages. Available fake-transport tests can support parsing, repository behavior, notifier transitions, and widget assertions for localized labels and confirmation states. After implementation, a distinct bounded review should check reachable failures, lifecycle handling, contract compatibility, and implementation residue, followed by formatting, analysis, and affected tests.

No code was inspected or changed, and no checks were run. Fake-transport results, when executed, would establish local behavior with fake data only. Staging authentication and live API compatibility remain unverified without credentials; Android rendering, lifecycle, and end-to-end behavior remain unverified without an Android target. Those limitations must remain explicit in the delivery handoff.
